guidance.claim: The risk register is standard across PMBOK, PRINCE2 and ISO Guide 73 — a record of information about identified risks.
For an assumption, state what is being relied on and how it will be checked. For a risk, state what could happen, its significance, and the response.
Distinct from Opportunities & Threats: there an outside condition is judged for planning; here anything inside or outside that could harm the work gets a response and someone to handle it.
Before committing, imagine the work has already failed and have each person write down why. This brings out risks people hesitate to raise.
The RFC tradition records drawbacks — known, accepted costs — separately from risks, which are uncertainties.
Where an approver or regulator will review the work, date each entry and name its owner and response, so the record can be audited.

sections.name: Risks and assumptions
sections.question: What could harm the work if it happened or proved wrong?

guidance.claim: List everyone who bears a cost, hazard or loss from the work, including people who never use what it produces, such as the neighbours of a building site.

If the work's effects fall only on those accountable for it, say so and leave the list empty for that reason. A blank list with no such note cannot show that anyone checked who else carries the work's risks.
For each party, record what claim it has to be heard, such as a legal right, a contract or direct harm. That claim decides whether a risk it carries can be accepted without asking it.
Distinct from Decision Authority & Approvals: a party here is heard and weighed; an approver there decides whether the work goes ahead. If the work needs their yes, list them there.

sections.name: Affected and interested parties
sections.question: Who does the work affect beyond those accountable for it?

guidance.claim: The counterweight to any target — latency, churn, quality, trust; burnout at personal scale.
Guardrails that protect the organisation, such as page-load time or revenue, are largely shared across experiments. Define them once, for the whole organisation, and reuse them in every effort.
Experimentation-heavy organisations formalise these as launch blockers; everywhere else they stay implicit until an incident. Write them down first.

Distinct from Input Metrics. Ask whether the number should move or hold: an input metric is pushed to move, a guardrail is held within its range. Neither the Business Model Canvas nor the Lean Canvas has a block for guardrails, so keep them in Success Metrics.

sections.name: Guardrail health metrics
sections.question: Which measures must stay within set ranges while we pursue other targets?

guidance.claim: Each wants an owner and a resolution path. An unowned question is a risk mislabelled.

Distinct from Risks & Assumptions: an open question is something to answer before a point can be settled; an assumption is a belief the work proceeds on and checks along the way. Proceeding without the answer turns the question into an assumption.
Compare the list across drafts: it should get shorter. A list that keeps growing means the work is not yet ready to settle.
Write 'none open' only when every question raised has been answered or recorded as an assumption, so a reader can tell it apart from a list nobody has drawn up.
